Error Budget and Error Propagation Review

Scope: src/pipeline.py (detection_and_photometry, calculate_zero_point, estimate_background in src/tools_pipeline.py), src/psf.py (perform_psf_photometry) and the calibration helpers in src/tools_pipeline.py (add_calibrated_magnitudes, apply_color_term_correction).

Method: read the implementation end to end, cross-checked against the published photutils formulas/source and against the current docs/PHOTOMETRY_FORMULAS.md, docs/features.rst and the README changelog. Line references are approximate and intended as signposts, not exact anchors.

1. Executive summary

The error budget is, overall, well constructed and internally consistent. The core chain

per-pixel error -> aperture flux error -> local-background term -> sigma_flux
                -> S/N, sigma_mag -> sigma_mag_calib (+ zero point)

uses a single flux for the magnitude, its error and the S/N, and each propagated term is dimensionally correct. The most important known failure modes (raw aperture sum used for the error while the magnitude used the background-corrected flux, missing local-background variance, rounded zero point, no zero-point error) have all been addressed and are covered by tests.

The remaining gaps are of two kinds:

  1. a small statistical inconsistency in the local-background term (a median is used for the value but the mean’s standard error for its uncertainty);

  2. unmodeled systematics that are not represented in any exported error at all: the aperture correction, the color-term correction, and the correlated nature of the zero-point error.

None of these invalidates the pipeline. They are worth fixing because they affect the same background-limited regime the project already invested in, and because two of them (aperture and color-term corrections) are the largest remaining contributions to the total photometric error budget at high S/N.

2. The error budget as implemented

2.1 Per-pixel error map

detection_and_photometry builds the map with photutils.utils.calc_total_error:

sigma_pix^2 = sigma_bkg,pix^2 + max(I_pix, 0) / g_eff

where sigma_bkg,pix = Background2D.background_rms (MAD-based estimator, MADStdBackgroundRMS), I_pix is the background-subtracted image (image_sub) and g_eff is the resolved effective gain.

This matches the photutils reference formula sigma_tot = sqrt(sigma_bkg^2 + I / g_eff) exactly. Verified against the photutils 3.0 source (photutils/utils/errors.py), including the documented behaviour that the Poisson term is dropped wherever data is negative (source_variance = np.maximum(source_variance, 0)), so background-subtracted sources with negative sky pixels get only the background term there. This is correct and is not a bug, but it is worth knowing.

2.2 Aperture flux and its error

aperture_photometry(image_sub, aperture, error=total_error, mask=mask, wcs=...) returns

aperture_sum_err = sqrt( sum_{aperture} total_error^2 )

with the pipeline mask (border + cosmic rays + satellite trails + NaNs) applied and the exact masked area returned through area_overlap.

2.3 Local background and its error

For aperture area A_ap and annulus area A_ann:

bkg_per_pixel   = sigma-clipped median of the annulus   (ApertureStats.median)
total_bkg       = bkg_per_pixel * A_ap
sigma_bkg_pixel = annulus_std / sqrt(A_ann)             <-- see finding F1
sigma_total_bkg = sigma_bkg_pixel * A_ap
flux            = aperture_sum - total_bkg
sigma_flux^2    = aperture_sum_err^2 + sigma_total_bkg^2

2.4 S/N, magnitude and magnitude error

S/N       = flux / sigma_flux          (flux errors > 0, else NaN)
mag_inst  = -2.5 * log10(flux * apcorr)
sigma_mag = 1.0857 * (sigma_flux * apcorr) / (flux * apcorr)
          = 1.0857 * sigma_flux / flux

The aperture correction cancels in the ratio, so S/N and sigma_mag are invariant under apcorr while the magnitude itself is not. This is consistent.

2.5 Calibrated magnitude error

sigma_mag_calib = sqrt( sigma_mag^2 + sigma_zp^2 + sigma_sys^2 )
sigma_zp        = 1.2533 * scatter / sqrt(N)      (median standard error)

sigma_zp is applied to every aperture_mag_err_* and psf_mag_err column in add_calibrated_magnitudes, at full precision.

2.6 PSF photometry

PSFPhotometry(...)(img, init_params=..., mask=..., error=error) receives the same total_error map, so flux_err is derived from the same per-pixel noise model as the aperture errors.

2.7 Numerical sanity check of the local-background term

For the default annulus r_in = 2r, r_out = 2.5r: A_ap / A_ann = 1 / (2.5^2 - 2.0^2) = 1/2.25 = 0.444, so the local-background term is sqrt(A_ap/A_ann) = 0.667 times the aperture sky-noise term. In quadrature this raises sigma_flux by sqrt(1 + 0.444) = 1.202, i.e. ~20% — matching the figure quoted in docs/PHOTOMETRY_FORMULAS.md. The documentation is correct.

4. Findings

Ranked by expected impact on the total error budget. No finding breaks the pipeline; all are incremental accuracy/consistency improvements.

F1 — Local-background error uses the mean standard error for a median (medium) — FIXED

Status: fixed. The annulus uncertainty now uses ApertureStats.median_err (with std / sqrt(A_ann) kept only as a fallback), and a regression test (TestPipelineErrorBudget::test_local_background_error_uses_median_error) guards it. docs/PHOTOMETRY_FORMULAS.md was updated to match.

Where: src/pipeline.py, annulus block (bkg_per_pixel_err = bkg_std / np.sqrt(annulus_area)), ~lines 1320–1340.

Issue: the value is ApertureStats.median (a sigma-clipped median) but the uncertainty uses the standard error of the mean, std / sqrt(A_ann). The standard error of a median is larger by sqrt(pi/2) = 1.2533. photutils exposes exactly the right quantity: ApertureStats.median_err is documented as the large-sample approximation sqrt(pi/2) * s / sqrt(n).

Impact: the local-background term is underestimated by ~25%. In the background-limited regime the total sigma_flux is then low by ~8% (the local term contributes a factor ~1.20 to the total; raising it by 1.2533 gives ~1.30 instead). This is the same class of bias that was fixed for the zero point, and it is the only remaining term in the budget that uses the wrong estimator.

Resolution: replaced bkg_std / sqrt(annulus_area) with np.asarray(annulus_stats.median_err, dtype=float), keeping the existing annulus_area fallback only when median_err is unavailable or non-finite.

F2 — Aperture-correction uncertainty is never propagated (medium) — FIXED

Status: fixed. A per-aperture systematic sigma_apcorr = 1.0857 · f_apcorr · |apcorr−1| / apcorr (with APCORR_SYSTEMATIC_FRACTION, default 0.20) is now added in quadrature to every aperture_mag_err_* and stored in apcorr_mag_err_*. The global SYSTEMATIC_MAG_ERR_FLOOR is now actually passed to add_calibrated_magnitudes via resolve_systematic_floor() (session state / RPP_SYSTEMATIC_MAG_ERR_FLOOR / module default). Tests: TestPipelineErrorBudget::test_error_budget_and_aperture_correction, test_add_calibrated_magnitudes_propagates_systematic_floor, test_resolve_systematic_floor_reads_environment.

Where: src/pipeline.py, apcorr block ~lines 1420–1440; the SYSTEMATIC_MAG_ERR_FLOOR constant at line 34.

Issue: apcorr = 1 / EE(r) is derived from the empirical ePSF (or a Gaussian fallback) and clamped to [1, 2]. The random part cancels in sigma_mag, but the systematic part does not: an error in EE(r) produces a magnitude offset that is completely absent from every exported error. The clamp at 2.0 also silently truncates a pathological correction, again with no error attached.

Additionally, SYSTEMATIC_MAG_ERR_FLOOR = 0.0 is defined in src/pipeline.py but is never passed to add_calibrated_magnitudes (which does accept a systematic_floor argument). The plumbing exists but is disconnected — dead code today.

Impact: at high S/N (where sigma_mag is small) the aperture-correction systematic dominates the realistic error budget but is invisible to the user.

Recommendation: either (a) estimate delta(EE) from the ePSF and propagate 1.0857 * delta(EE)/EE into sigma_mag or into the systematic floor, or (b) at minimum wire SYSTEMATIC_MAG_ERR_FLOOR through to add_calibrated_magnitudes and document the assumed floor. Note the clamp in the documentation either way.

F3 — Color-term-corrected magnitudes carry no error (medium) — FIXED

Status: fixed. fit_color_term_correction now returns the fit parameter covariance and standard errors, and apply_color_term_correction writes color_term_offset_err plus a *_colorcorr_err column √(σ_mag_calib² + σ_color_term_offset²) for every corrected magnitude (with filter-prefixed aliases). Tests: test_apply_color_term_correction_appends_new_columns_and_keeps_legacy, test_colorcorr_err_without_baseline_error_is_fit_only, test_fit_color_term_reports_parameter_uncertainties.

Where: src/tools_pipeline.py, apply_color_term_correction, ~lines 226–290.

Issue: the function appends *_colorcorr magnitudes and trace fields (color_term_offset, color_term_value, …) but never writes a *_colorcorr_err column, and the color-term coefficient/intercept uncertainty from fit_color_term_correction is not propagated. The *_colorcorr loop also deliberately skips existing error columns.

Impact: users who select *_colorcorr magnitudes for science get no error for them; the parallel baseline errors do not apply because the offset shifts the magnitude but does not change sigma_mag in the current model.

Recommendation: export *_colorcorr_err derived from the baseline error plus the color-term fit uncertainty (coefficient standard error times the color offset from color_ref), and document that the color term is not a random per-source error.

F4 — Zero-point scatter is biased low by the outlier cuts (low–medium) — FIXED

Status: fully fixed. calculate_zero_point now takes the scatter for σ_zp from the sigma-clipped sample before the ±0.5 mag hard cut (which truncates the tails), keeping the truncated value only as a reported diagnostic (zero_point_scatter_kept). Both scatter estimates and N are stored in st.session_state["zero_point_diagnostics"]. Separately, add_calibrated_magnitudes exports every magnitude error as a total plus explicit *_mag_err_*_random and *_mag_err_*_correlated components with filter-prefixed aliases. Test: TestZeroPointCalibration::test_zero_point_uncertainty_uses_untrimmed_scatter.

Where: src/pipeline.py, calculate_zero_point, sigma-clip + |residual| <= 0.5 mag block, ~lines 1700–1760.

Issue: sigma_zp = 1.2533 * scatter / sqrt(N) uses the scatter of the trimmed residual distribution. The explicit |residual| <= 0.5 mag hard cut removes the wings, so scatter — and therefore sigma_zp — is biased low (the code comment already acknowledges this). In addition, the zero-point error is a common systematic shared by every source in the field, yet it is added in quadrature per source as if it were independent.

Impact: sigma_mag_calib is slightly optimistic; for ensemble/relative work the correlated component behaves differently from the random component.

Recommendation: document the bias explicitly (it already is, in part) and consider reporting the untrimmed RMS as a diagnostic column. If absolute calibration matters, expose a flag distinguishing the random (sigma_mag) from the systematic (sigma_zp) part rather than only their quadrature sum.

F5 — Constant-background fallback uses a non-robust RMS (low) — FIXED

Status: fixed. _constant_background now uses stdfunc="mad_std", matching the normal Background2D path. Test: TestBackgroundRobustness::test_constant_fallback_rms_is_mad_based.

Where: src/tools_pipeline.py, _constant_background, ~line 1592.

Issue: the last-resort model uses sigma_clipped_stats(...)[2], the plain sigma-clipped standard deviation, whereas the normal path uses the MAD estimator. On the crowded frames that trigger this fallback, the plain std is inflated by undetected sources (the documented reason MADStdBackgroundRMS was adopted).

Impact: in exactly the fallback regime the per-pixel sigma_bkg — and hence every flux error — can be inflated by up to ~2x.

Recommendation: use the MAD-based RMS in _constant_background too, for consistency.

F6 — Detection threshold uses a non-robust global std (low) — FIXED

Status: fixed. Both the fwhm_fit noise estimate and the detection_and_photometry fallback now use stdfunc="mad_std", so the detection threshold and the error model use the same robust noise estimate.

Where: src/pipeline.py, sigma_clipped_stats(image_sub, sigma=3.0) feeding DAOStarFinder(threshold=(threshold_sigma + 0.5) * clipped_std), ~lines 1215–1230.

Issue: the detection threshold is set from the global sigma-clipped std, which is inflated by sources in crowded fields, rather than from the MAD-based noise that the error budget uses.

Impact: the effective detection threshold is higher than the requested threshold_sigma in crowded fields; faint sources are lost. It is a sensitivity/bias issue rather than a propagated-error issue.

Recommendation: derive the threshold from the MAD-based global RMS (or the median of the background_rms map) so detection and the error model agree.

F7 — PSF photometry has no PSF-mismatch or local-background term (low) — FIXED

Status: fixed. perform_psf_photometry builds one LocalBackground (sigma-clipped median annulus, 2×–3× FWHM) and uses it in two places:

  • ePSF build — the local background is subtracted from a copy of the image around each PSF star before extract_stars, so the empirical PSF is not built from sky-contaminated cutouts;

  • per-source fits — the background is evaluated with the pipeline mask and passed as the local_bkg column of the PSF-fitting init_params (with the estimator as a fallback). Sources with a fully masked/off-frame annulus fall back to no subtraction instead of a NaN fit.

Test: TestPsfApertureCoherency::test_psf_local_background_recovers_flux_with_constant_sky — the sky-induced flux bias drops from ×2.49 (no local background) to ×1.001 across the ensemble. A PSF-model mismatch can still remain on real, PSF-varying frames, but the background pedestal no longer drives it.

Where: src/psf.py, PSFPhotometry(...) construction ~line 1012; the local_bkg argument is not passed.

Issue: PSF fluxes are fitted on image_sub (global model already subtracted) with no explicit local background fit and no allowance for PSF model mismatch. flux_err faithfully reflects the per-pixel noise model but not these systematics, so PSF errors can be optimistic in nebulous/crowded fields.

Recommendation: consider local_bkg (e.g. the annulus median already computed for the aperture) and/or a PSF-mismatch term; at minimum document that the PSF error is a purely statistical estimate.

F8 — Centroiding error is not propagated (low) — FIXED

Status: fixed. The aperture flux error now includes a centroid-position term. sigma_pos = sigma_PSF / S/N (floored at 0.01 px, capped at 0.5×FWHM) and the flux change for a one-sigma displacement is measured directly by re-measuring the aperture shifted ±sigma_pos along x and y (so real PSF asymmetry/ellipticity is captured, unlike a symmetric-Gaussian derivative), sigma_centroid = 0.5·√(ΔF_x² + ΔF_y²). It is folded into aperture_sum_bkg_corr_err_* and exported as centroid_flux_err_X_X. Tests: every end-to-end budget test now verifies the full decomposition σ_flux² = σ_ap² + σ_bkg² + σ_centroid².

Issue: the aperture flux error accounts for per-pixel noise, the local background and (via area_overlap) the masked area, but not the uncertainty in the source position. For small apertures and undersampled PSFs, centroid error is a real contribution.

Recommendation: optional secondary term, or document it as a known omission.

F9 — Effective-gain fallback of 1 is conservative but not neutral (info)

As documented, with data in ADU and an unknown true gain g, setting g_eff = 1 overestimates the source Poisson variance by g, i.e. bright-source magnitude errors by up to sqrt(g). The ordering (header -> user -> empirical -> 1) and the BUNIT check are sound. No change needed; keep the warning.

F10 — Naming / observability nits (info) — FIXED

  • The misleading zero_point_error column was renamed to zero_point_scatter (calibrator scatter), and the formal zero_point_std is now stored alongside it in the matched table.

  • The documentation now states explicitly that the zero point is anchored to the aperture-corrected instrumental_mag_*, while instrumental_mag_bkg_corr_* is the uncorrected diagnostic reference.

  • ee_fraction_X_X is now exported next to apcorr_X_X, so the correction is auditable (a large apcorr is traceable to a poorly-enclosed aperture).

5. Test coverage assessment

tests/test_photometry.py already contains a dedicated TestPipelineErrorBudget class with end-to-end checks that:

  • S/N equals flux / sigma_flux for the background-corrected flux;

  • sigma_mag uses the same flux as the magnitude;

  • the local-background term is folded in (sigma_flux > aperture_sum_err);

  • the aperture correction is >= 1, bounded, and larger for the smaller aperture;

  • the real ePSF path produces the stored apcorr.

TestErrorPropagation covers sigma_mag_calib = sqrt(sigma_inst^2 + sigma_zp^2) and the default (instrumental-only) case. TestGainResolution, TestEffectiveGainEstimation, TestCosmicRayMasking, TestUnreliablePhotometryCut and TestBright/FaintSource cover the adjacent budget terms.

Gaps worth adding tests for:

  1. median_err-based local-background term (F1) — a regression test asserting sigma_flux uses the median standard error.

  2. systematic_floor actually affecting exported errors (F2).

  3. *_colorcorr_err existence and value (F3).

  4. _constant_background RMS is MAD-based (F5).

  5. Zero-point scatter vs formal uncertainty distinguishable in the output (F10).

6. Suggested follow-ups (in priority order)

  1. F1 — switch the local-background uncertainty to ApertureStats.median_err.

  2. F2 — propagate/report the aperture-correction systematic; wire or remove SYSTEMATIC_MAG_ERR_FLOOR.

  3. F3 — export *_colorcorr_err with color-term fit uncertainty.

  4. F5 / F6 — use MAD-based noise for the constant fallback and the detection threshold, for consistency with the error model.

  5. F4 / F7 / F8 — document the correlated/systematic components and the PSF/centroid omissions, or model them.

  6. Update docs/PHOTOMETRY_FORMULAS.md to match whatever is changed.

8. Post-review updates (v1.8.5)

This section records changes made after the review above. They concern PSF photometry reliability and the ePSF geometry rather than the calibrated error budget, which is unchanged.

  • PSF star selection no longer uses the sqrt(flux) approximation for a hard 50% S/N cut, and the saturation filter no longer rejects the brightest unsaturated stars. On a clean 121-star field this goes from 14 selected stars (below the 15-star minimum, so the whole PSF step was skipped) to 49, with photometry on all 121 sources.

  • ePSF geometry: the fitting region is rounded (int(3·FWHM) was biasing the effective radius by up to half a pixel), the ePSF is extracted from a larger ≈5× FWHM cutout so its wings are not truncated/normalised away, the model centre is (N − 1)/2, and the aperture-correction model is the exact object used for the fits (including any re-centering).

  • PSF-vs-aperture diagnostic: check_psf_aperture_consistency() reports the median psf_mag − aperture_mag per aperture and warns above PSF_APERTURE_CONSISTENCY_THRESHOLD (0.15 mag). This makes the class of ePSF shape/normalisation offset discussed for PSF photometry directly observable instead of having to be inferred from the catalog.

  • Crowded local background was investigated as a possible “double subtraction” of the background. It is not a real flux bias in photutils 3.0 (per-source local_bkg is subtracted once from each source’s own cutout); zeroing it for overlapping sources would bias crowded fluxes ~5-7% high, so no guard was applied. See docs/PHOTOMETRY_FORMULAS.md for the numbers.
